newsitem.title: USA: Dakotah sees Q1 down vs prior year.
newsitem.headline: Dakotah sees Q1 down vs prior year.

text.p: Dakotah Inc said Tuesday it expects sales and earnings for the first quarter will be down compared with the year-ago period.

But the company, which makes decorative pillows, table linens and other home accessories, said it expects sales for all of 1997 will be up from 1996. The company did not make an earnings projection for the year.
In the year-ago first quarter, Dakotah earned $2,000, but posted no earnings per share.

The company said the first quarter results will be down from a year ago due to moving its warehouse and distribution center and Webster pillow filling manufacturing operation and the loss of operating hours related to severe winter weather.
However, Dakotah is expecting continued increases in annual net sales, he added.
"Our open orders for 1997 are up significantly over 1996," Jones said.

Earlier, Dakotah reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.17 a share on sales of $15.0 million, up from year-ago earnings of $0.05 a share on sales of $10.8 million. For the year, it earned $0.24 a sahre on sales of $41.6 million, up from 1995 earnings of $0.13 a share on sales of $30.9 million.

"Dakotah is very pleased with our ability to increase market share and develop new markets for our customers," George Whyte, chairman, said in a statement. "While 1996 was slightly better than 1995 for the home fashion textile industry, I still do not believe our industry is operating at its long-term sustainable demand levels. I am expecting sales in 1997 to be better than 1996 for Dakotah and most of our industry."
